claims.text: Controlled atomic-size mismatch increases lattice distortion in lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Increased lattice distortion generates localized internal strain fields.
Localized internal strain fields impede dislocation glide.
Impeded dislocation glide enhances mechanical strength and yield strength.
Localized internal strain fields promote nucleation or formation of a compact, dense, adherent passivating oxide layer.
A compact, adherent passivating oxide layer improves corrosion resistance.
A compact, adherent passivating oxide layer improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
An Al–Ti–V–Cr–Fe-based matrix with engineered atomic-size mismatch can remain lightweight.
Substituting elements with different atomic radii can vary lattice distortion while preserving a lightweight alloy.
The high-distortion variant will have higher yield strength than the low-distortion baseline under conditions where distortion remains effective.
The high-distortion variant will have a lower corrosion rate than the low-distortion baseline.
The high-distortion variant will form a more compact and adherent oxide layer than the low-distortion baseline.
Above approximately 800°C, thermal vibrations reduce the effectiveness of lattice-distortion-induced strain fields.
Above approximately 800°C, the mechanical-strength and passivation benefits of lattice distortion diminish.
The proposed lattice-distortion benefits should persist up to approximately 800°C.
